subject: Converting legacy enterprise contract to AWS Private Offer - term mapping & approvals
messages:
From: Anna Sanders <anna.sanders@quantifyhealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>; Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Quantify Health Procurement <procure@quantifyhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Converting our existing legacy contract to an AWS Private Offer (term questions)

Hi Mina / Vanessa,

Thanks again for the product demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency/cost profile. We have an existing multi-year agreement with Redwood (signed 2024) and our procurement/legal teams prefer to buy via AWS Private Offer to align billing and internal purchasing controls. A few asks from our side:

- Can we map our legacy 36-month commitment to a private offer with the same pricing schedule?
- Procurement needs clarity on buyer approval routing (multiple business units). Will AWS treat this as one consolidated buyer or separate account-level approvals?
- Legal has redlined one clause related to data retention; I’ve attached our redlines.

We’d like to close this in July. Can you outline the operational steps and approvals so we can present to our CFO?

Thanks,
Anna Sanders
Director, IT Procurement
Quantify Health

Attachment: quantify_health_redlines_0627.pdf

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Anna Sanders <anna.sanders@quantifyhealth.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Converting our existing legacy contract to an AWS Private Offer (term questions)

Hi Anna — great to hear. We can definitely help migrate the commercial terms into an AWS Private Offer, but there are a few practical notes so expectations are aligned:

1) Term length & legacy mapping: AWS Marketplace private offers support a range of durations. We generally map legacy commitments to an equivalent private offer but need to confirm whether your original SKUs and committed usage align to what will be provisioned in the private offer (there are SKU/plan mappings that can affect unit pricing).

2) Buyer approvals: AWS treats the Private Offer as a contract tied to the buyer account(s). If you want a single consolidated contract across multiple business units we will need to list each buyer account and the primary approver for each in the offer configuration. That can add time for procurement sign-off.

3) Legal redlines: thanks for the PDF. I’ve looped in our legal lead, Laura Bennett, to review the redlines and advise which clauses are AWS-sensitive (e.g., liability caps vs. marketplace terms).

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll draft an operational checklist (who signs what and when) and share the Redwood Private Offer template.
- Vanessa will confirm pricing alignment and any concessions for legacy customers.
- Vivek will coordinate approvals with our AWS marketplace specialist if we need seller-assisted routing.

Can you confirm target billing cadence (annual vs. monthly) and whether the CFO needs any special amortization language?

Best,
Mina Haddad
Head of Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_private_offer_template.pdf

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>; Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Converting our existing legacy contract to an AWS Private Offer (term questions)

Quick notes from pricing ops after reviewing Anna’s redlines:

- Pricing: we can preserve the legacy effective rate for the first 24 months and then move to the current list/usage tier for months 25-36; this is the simplest way to respect prior economics while keeping a clear renewal path. If Quantify needs equal rate across 36 months, we’ll need a sponsor-level discount approval (finance + RevOps).
- Billing cadence: annual billing is straightforward; AWS private offer with annual invoices maps cleanly to their procurement process. Monthly invoicing via marketplace is possible but requires additional buyer account-level billing setup.
- Approvals: if this will span multiple buyer accounts, we recommend a master purchaser account be listed to speed the AWS-side acceptance. Otherwise expect ~2 weeks for each additional buyer approval.

I’ve attached a short procurement-checklist we use internally to track buyer account listing, DocuSign steps, and who needs to countersign.

-Vanessa
Director, Marketplace Partnerships
Attachment: procurement-checklist.xlsx

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: AWS Seller Support <aws-seller-support@amazon.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 10:09:00 -07:00
Subject: Request: seller-assisted Private Offer creation for Quantify Health (RDW-2027-QH-047)

Hi AWS team,

We have a customer (Quantify Health, account IDs listed in the procurement checklist) who requests a seller-assisted Private Offer that mirrors an existing Redwood enterprise contract (36 months). We need guidance on:

- Best practice to list multiple buyer accounts under one offer vs. separate offers per BU
- How AWS enforces term length when a private offer is created from legacy manual contracts
- Any marketplace limitations on passing through legacy concessions (e.g., multi-year rate locks)

Relevant artifacts: procurement-checklist.xlsx (attached) and the redwood_private_offer_template.pdf. Please advise estimated SLA for offer activation and what approval emails will be sent to buyer accounts.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Anna Sanders <anna.sanders@quantifyhealth.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Jul 2027 14:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Converting our existing legacy contract to an AWS Private Offer (term questions)

Hi Anna — I reviewed your redlines. A few quick points from Redwood legal:

- Data retention clause: we can accept the proposed shorter retention window, but we need to confirm there are no AWS marketplace terms that conflict (some marketplace-driven telemetry or audit logging obligations cannot be shortened). I’ve flagged this for AWS Seller Support.
- Liability / indemnity: we cannot expand liability beyond our standard marketplace caps. If Quantify requires different liability limits, that will need an escalated commercial exception and finance sign-off.
- Signature flow: DocuSign via the private offer is acceptable. We will not countersign separately outside of the marketplace unless necessary for governance reasons.

I’ll prepare redlines that are material and identify which items require escalations. Karthik — can you confirm whether finance is prepared to approve a full 36-month rate lock or the 24/12 split Vanessa suggested?

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Associate General Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Anna Sanders <anna.sanders@quantifyhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Jul 2027 16:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Converting our existing legacy contract to an AWS Private Offer (term questions)

Team / Anna — quick commercial decision so Quantify can move forward: finance can approve the 24-month effective-rate concession followed by a renewal-rate for months 25-36 (this avoids a long-term rate lock liability on Redwood). If Quantify insists on a full 36-month flat rate we need a formal discount exception and partner-sponsorship (will add ~10 business days).

Operationally we recommend:
- Proceed with seller-assisted private offer listing each buyer account with a master payer to speed approval.
- Laura to finalize redlines that are AWS-compatible.
- Mina/Vanessa to issue the private offer draft and share DocuSign link once AWS confirms account listing.

Anna, if this approach works I’ll ask RevOps to approve the concession and we can push a DocuSign Private Offer to you early next week.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
